correctness.rationale: The kernel binomial(n+k,k)∫(1−t)^n t^k dμ is bounded by Schur on compact support in (0,1), and self-adjoint by reflection symmetry. The compact-support Laplace principle applies even to singular measures. For s=max(S∩(0,1/2)), h=s(1−s), diagonal logarithmic growth is log(4h) per index, while the binomial/KL expression for entry (m−floor(sm),floor(sm)) has m-th log limit zero because t=s is in support. The normalized off-diagonal therefore has m-th log growth −log(2√h)>0; its 2×2 principal minor is negative for large m. For μ=(δ_s+δ_(1−s))/2, local binomial Stirling gives prefactor 1/(2√2 h^(1/4)); δ_(1/2) is a nonnegative Gram kernel. Independently evaluated four exact rational negative minors; these tests do not prove the universal Laplace step.
